newsitem.title: LEBANON: Jordanian said arrested for anti-Syrian attacks.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian said arrested for anti-Syrian attacks.

text.p: The manager of Beirut's Marriott Hotel said on Saturday a Jordanian employee reported arrested by Lebanese security forces for alleged links to anti-Syrian attacks disappeared 15 days ago and has not been seen since.
General Manager Sam Ibrahim said financial controller Derar al-Karmi, a Jordanian, left the hotel in West Beirut "with unknown persons" on January 3 and has not come back since.
"All I know is he left the hotel on January 3 at about 5.15 p.m. with unknown persons. We don't know where he is now," Ibrahim told Reuters. He said Karmi was in his 40s but did not elaborate.
He was commenting on Beirut newspaper reports on Saturday that Karmi was arrested by Lebanese security forces on January 3 on suspicion of links to recent attacks on Syrian targets.

Ad-Diyar daily, quoting official sources, said Karmi was arrested on suspicion of links to a machinegun attack on December 18 on a van carrying Syrian workers in the Christian area of Tabarja north of Beirut in which the driver was killed.

An-Nahar daily, quoting a recent report by the Kuwaiti daily al-Anbaa, said Karmi was arrested but it was not clear if he was being questioned over the Tabarja incident or the December 31 bus bombing in Damascus that killed 11 people.
Syria has accused Israel of being behind the Damascus blast, an allegation denied by Israel.
Asked about Karmi's arrest, prosecutor-general Adnan Adoum said: "I can't confirm or deny this because I am not aware of it personally and did not give orders to arrest anyone."
Some 48 Lebanese people were arrested after the Tabarja attack but were freed later.
Damascus is Beirut's main foreign power broker with 35,000 troops stationed over two thirds of Lebanon.
